feed.title: RSS System Design Articles
feed.subtitle: System design decisions, architectures and failures from engineering blogs. Summaries and Classifier leverages AI; may contain errors.

entry.title: Agentic Development: The Fun Part Was Never the Typing
entry.summary: An Atomic Object developer argues agentic development moves effort from typing to design, citing a Power BI report builder that an agent built test-first into a thirty-thousand-line web application.

entry.title: Write End-to-End Tests in Your Backend’s Language
entry.summary: Atomic Object argues for writing browser end-to-end tests in the backend's language so test data setup can use domain models, shown with a FastAPI and Python Playwright example.

entry.title: Architecting Secure Identity: Extending Auth0 PrivateLink with Intelligent Gateways
entry.summary: Auth0 describes an intelligent gateway pattern that terminates a single outbound PrivateLink connection at an API gateway or reverse proxy and routes traffic to isolated VPCs.

entry.title: Everybody Thinks Login Is Easy. Until It Is Not
entry.summary: Auth0 argues that login grows from a form into an identity model, covering account linking, recovery, session revocation, enterprise organizations and delegation to AI agents.

entry.title: ID-JAG, Explained: The New OAuth Grant for Cross-App Access
entry.summary: Auth0 explains ID-JAG, a new OAuth grant where an enterprise identity provider issues a signed assertion that lets an app or agent get an access token for another app without per-pair consent.

entry.title: Multi-Tenant SaaS Apps with Auth0 Organizations — Part One
entry.summary: Auth0 uses a fictional SaaS company to show how Auth0 Organizations model tenants for B2B login, enterprise SSO routing, tenant switching and org-scoped roles.

entry.title: Securing AI Agents with Auth0 CIMD and Token Exchange
entry.summary: Auth0 describes securing AI agents as third-party OAuth clients with strict mode, Client ID Metadata Documents for registration and token exchange for delegation chains.

entry.title: Announcing AWS Lambda Web Functions
entry.summary: AWS announced Lambda Web Functions, which run standard port-listening HTTP servers on Lambda with up to 128 concurrent requests per environment and billing on active CPU time.

entry.title: Geometry Nodes Workshop: September 2026
entry.summary: Blender's Geometry Nodes team summarizes its September 2026 workshop, covering recent features and design decisions for modal node tools, exposed bakes, lists, physics and node layout.

entry.title: 2026 Birthday week: network performance update
entry.summary: Cloudflare reports it is fastest in 74% of the 1,000 largest networks, up from 60%, and adds Challenge Page measurements to its error-page based methodology.

entry.title: AI Search is now generally available
entry.summary: Cloudflare made AI Search generally available, adding native image embeddings alongside captions, OCR for scanned PDFs, 10 MiB files and usage-based pricing from November 1, 2026.

entry.title: Announcing Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway – expanding access to Cloudflare’s privacy-preserving infrastructure
entry.summary: Cloudflare launched a closed beta OHTTP Gateway that decapsulates Oblivious HTTP requests for apps behind Cloudflare, complementing its renamed OHTTP Relay.

entry.title: Beyond the patch: Protecting your NetScaler gateway against future vulnerabilities
entry.summary: Cloudflare explains how to protect Citrix NetScaler and other public login gateways after actively exploited vulnerabilities, using access policies, WAF inspection and restricted origin connections.

entry.title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
entry.summary: Cloudflare launched a post-quantum GeoKey Manager in closed beta that wraps customer decryption keys so only servers in a chosen region can unwrap them, using hybrid ML-KEM-768 and X25519.

entry.title: Deno is joining Cloudflare
entry.summary: Cloudflare announces that the Deno team is joining it to make self-hosting the open-source Workers runtime workerd practical, and explains its reasoning on platform lock-in.

entry.title: Deploy with Void
entry.summary: Cloudflare and VoidZero open-sourced Void, a Vite-based platform, SDK and CLI that let companies host internal and agent-built apps on Cloudflare without giving every employee cloud access.

entry.title: Identify AI model overuse with User Insights
entry.summary: Cloudflare added task context to AI Gateway User Insights, including a model overkill view that flags requests sent to models more capable than the task needs.

entry.title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models
entry.summary: Cloudflare previewed Clairic, an extraction model on Workers AI that returns typed values, estimates and forecasts with confidence scores in a single pass instead of generating tokens.

entry.title: Introducing Clef-omni with full multimodality, plus a faster Clef and a cheaper Clef-flash
entry.summary: Cloudflare released Clef-omni, a decision model that takes audio, video, image and text in one call, and made Clef faster and Clef-flash cheaper.

entry.title: Introducing Clef: our open-source decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
entry.summary: Cloudflare released Clef and Clef-flash, open-source decision models on Workers AI that return typed classifications with probabilities, and a reinforcement learning fine-tuning service.

entry.title: Introducing Cloudflare Basin: an open, serverless data platform, now generally available
entry.summary: Cloudflare renamed its data platform Basin and made it generally available: Pipelines, Catalog and SQL on Apache Iceberg and R2, with ingestion up to 3GB/s per stream.

entry.title: Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust
entry.summary: Cloudflare, VoidZero and Owner.com are building tsrs, a faithful Rust port of the TypeScript compiler that is up to 8x faster and uses about 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0.

entry.title: Monetization Gateway beta: charge AI agents for consumption with HTTP 402
entry.summary: Cloudflare's Monetization Gateway closed beta lets site owners charge AI agents per request for websites, APIs, MCP tools or datasets using HTTP 402 Payment Required.

entry.title: Pay Per Use: when AI uses your work, you should get paid
entry.summary: Cloudflare's Pay Per Use beta lets AI companies offer a price for each use of a publisher's content, report each use through an API, and have Cloudflare bill buyers and pay publishers.

entry.title: Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down
entry.summary: Cloudflare describes five data pipeline changes, from splitting a monolithic schema to zstd compression, replication, sampling and aggregation, that deferred about two and a half years of hardware growth.

entry.title: Support for modern cryptographic algorithms in Workers
entry.summary: Cloudflare Workers added opt-in post-quantum ML-KEM and ML-DSA algorithms to Web Crypto, backed by BoringSSL in workerd, behind a compatibility flag while the specification moves.

entry.title: The Internet has a second audience
entry.summary: Cloudflare argues that agents now form a second web audience, citing request growth from 63 to 115 million per second, and describes controls, payments and cost reductions for serving them.

entry.title: The keys to the Internet change on October 11. Are you ready?
entry.summary: Cloudflare explains the October 11, 2026 DNS root key-signing key rollover, how resolvers learn the new key, and the readiness test it built using RFC 8509.

entry.title: Biomedical Imaging's Real Bottleneck Is the Data, Not the Model
entry.summary: Databricks argues that biomedical imaging AI is limited by data access and governance rather than models, and outlines a governed data foundation for imaging, training and validation.

entry.title: Built for Agents: The Case for Spark Declarative Pipelines
entry.summary: Databricks benchmarked 528 agent-built data pipelines and found declarative Spark Declarative Pipelines cheaper, faster and leaner than procedural PySpark for coding agents.

entry.title: Closing the Binary Blind Spot: Domain-Knowledge Injection for LLM Malware Triage in npm Packages
entry.summary: Databricks researchers tested how LLMs triage npm packages hiding malicious native binaries and improved detection by injecting precomputed capability profiles into the prompt.

entry.title: From post-training to production: How TinyFish runs its web-native model on Databricks AI Runtime
entry.summary: TinyFish post-trains, evaluates and serves its web-native agent model on Databricks, reporting a 77.6% task-success rate and serving cost per agent run.

entry.title: How California built its Behavioral Health Public County Profile on Databricks
entry.summary: California's Department of Health Care Services built a public Behavioral Health County Profile dashboard on Databricks that brings data from all 58 counties into one place.

entry.title: How HP Is Building an AI-Ready CDP with Databricks CustomerLake
entry.summary: HP consolidated its marketing data into a governed lakehouse and adopted Databricks CustomerLake as its CDP, cutting audience creation from 2-3 months to 2 hours.

entry.title: How our AI Research team uses AI Runtime
entry.summary: Databricks' AI Research team explains how it trains models up to nearly a trillion parameters on AI Runtime, including GPU node health checks, container reuse and experiment tracking.

entry.title: Introducing Agent Memory on Databricks
entry.summary: Databricks introduced Agent Memory on Agent Bricks, based on its MemCurrent research, reporting triple the agent pass rate on enterprise tasks with 31% fewer tokens.

entry.title: Introducing Funke: Native HL7v2 Parsing on Databricks
entry.summary: Databricks open-sourced Funke, an HL7v2 parser that loads healthcare messages into native Spark types with the full hierarchy, as a declarative medallion pipeline replacing Smolder.

entry.title: Introducing Private Network Gateway
entry.summary: Databricks introduced Private Network Gateway, a managed encrypted gateway from serverless compute into one delegated customer subnet, so private databases and APIs become reachable without per-resource endpoints.

entry.title: Lakebase and Agentic SDLC: Branching Databases for Coding Agents
entry.summary: Databricks shows a development workflow where each coding agent's Git worktree and each pull request gets its own copy-on-write Lakebase Postgres branch.

entry.title: MemCurrent: Designing Persistent Memory for Production Agents
entry.summary: Databricks describes MemCurrent, a memory architecture for production agents combining episodic and derived memory, evaluated on public benchmarks and an internal benchmark from real Genie sessions.

entry.title: Real-time energy trading and analytics on Databricks
entry.summary: Databricks outlines a real-time energy trading architecture where streamed market data lands in Lakebase for the live desk and feeds analytics, ML signals and history from one copy.

entry.title: Reducing Qwen training time by 6x on AI Runtime
entry.summary: Databricks cut fine-tuning time for Qwen 3.8 27B from 7 hours 44 minutes to 1 hour 17 minutes using fused kernels and changes to batching, tokenization and padding.

entry.title: Reducing the noise: How Atlassian built an OCSF security lakehouse on Databricks
entry.summary: Atlassian standardized security logs on the OCSF schema and built a self-service security lakehouse on Databricks, handling 44 billion events a day and powering 500+ detection signals.

entry.title: Sizing Lakebase Search: lessons from a real app and 4 million passages
entry.summary: Databricks measured how search inside Lakebase Postgres behaves for the Slide Hub app and a 4-million-passage corpus, covering compute limits, candidate pools, cold starts, recall and cost.

entry.title: Solving defense supply chain visibility through governed data sharing
entry.summary: Databricks proposes a federated, governed data exchange so the US Department of War can see supplier cost and supply chain data without central repositories or direct ERP connections.

entry.title: The AI Bill is coming
entry.summary: Databricks co-founder Patrick Wendell explains how AI coding agent costs spiraled at Databricks and how a central gateway, model routing and spend visibility cut unit costs by up to 90%.

entry.title: The Fraud Analyst AI Coworker: Detecting Telecom Fraud in Real-Time on One Platform
entry.summary: Databricks argues that telecom fraud signals are split across six or seven systems synced by batch jobs, and outlines a unified real-time architecture and AI analyst assistant.

entry.title: The new economics of AI cost management
entry.summary: A Databricks engineer leading Unity Gateway explains how organizations should attribute, control and optimize AI spend, from request tags to on-demand context and model routing.

entry.title: Transactions are Generally Available, advancing warehousing on the Lakehouse
entry.summary: Databricks made multi-statement, multi-table transactions generally available on Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg, with row-level concurrency and examples from Fivetran and Accolade.

entry.title: Unlocking Data Portability: Preventing Catalog Lock-in with REGISTER and UNREGISTER APIs
entry.summary: Databricks explains how Iceberg REST catalog REGISTER and the UNREGISTER endpoint it contributed let tables move between catalogs without copying data or causing split-brain commits.

entry.title: What is HTAP? A plain-English guide to hybrid transactional/analytical processing
entry.summary: Databricks explains how HTAP systems combine transactional and analytical processing, their trade-offs, and how TiDB, AlloyDB and Lakebase's lake-based approach implement them.

entry.title: Can Agentic AI Find the Security Vulnerabilities Other Tests Miss?
entry.summary: Erlang Solutions describes an agent-driven security review of the Erlang/OTP repository that reported about 20 previously unknown potentially severe vulnerabilities, and how such findings must be validated.

entry.title: How Meta Built Forum With AI-Native Engineering
entry.summary: Meta describes how a small team built its Forum app with AI agents running the plan-build-test loop under engineer supervision, gated by automated verification.

entry.title: Explainable AI: If You Can’t Evaluate It, Can You Trust It?
entry.summary: Feedzai compared eight SHAP formulations with offline metrics and a study of 37 analysts, finding that explanations changed analyst confidence without improving decision accuracy.

entry.title: From a Trace to Money Flow: How we built an interactive visualization to uncover money laundering
entry.summary: Feedzai explains how it redesigned a fraud analysis graph into a Money Flow visualization that combines a network, a table and a sankey diagram to trace laundering networks.

entry.title: The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure
entry.summary: GitHub explains how it moved copies of 99.99999% of repositories to Azure and how per-reference quorums will move the busiest remaining ones despite a 25 ms round trip.

entry.title: GitHub availability report: September 2026
entry.summary: GitHub's September 2026 availability report covers two incidents, including a cleanup job that exhausted a shared database's connections, and progress moving production services to Azure.

entry.title: Secret protection must scale with software
entry.summary: GitHub's secret protection lead shares nine quarters of push data and introduces a fine-tuned classifier, built with Microsoft, that extends push protection to unstructured secrets.

entry.title: GrabMart data for faster disease outbreak detection
entry.summary: Grab describes an early-stage, undeployed concept for detecting disease outbreaks from aggregated GrabMart over-the-counter product demand, with privacy and governance controls.

entry.title: Smarter personalization: How property data helps us understand user price sensitivity
entry.summary: Grab describes an unimplemented proposal to add residential property values to user profiles, using LLM-structured property data, building-level price estimates and clustered affluence tiers.

entry.title: Designing A Secure Voice AI System for Regulated Industries
entry.summary: Haptik lists ten design principles for secure voice AI in banking, insurance and healthcare, covering data flow, authentication, least privilege, tenant isolation, RAG, tools and failure handling.

entry.title: Mitigating memorization in LLMs
entry.summary: A Jane Street intern measured when LLMs succeed by recalling memorized outcomes and tested mitigations such as divergence decoding, distillation and synthetic rewrites on a cricket dataset.

entry.title: What the SP interns have wrought, 2026 edition
entry.summary: Jane Street describes Strategy and Product intern projects, including modeling loan fee expense and allocating financing costs to desks, and managing risk-limit overrides on special dates.

entry.title: What the TDOE interns have wrought, 2026 edition
entry.summary: Jane Street describes three Trading Desk Operations intern projects, including a system that flags discrepancies between internal voice-trade records and the public tape.

entry.title: Decreasing CI Build times up to 50% by caching derived data using github actions.
entry.summary: Kogan cut its iOS CI build time from over 30 minutes to about 15 by caching Xcode derived data in GitHub Actions, keyed by the nearest develop commit.

entry.title: Introducing The Developer Workflow Team
entry.summary: Mozilla introduces its Developer Workflow team, explains why it scoped itself beyond the build system, and lists its planned build migrations and what it chose not to do.

entry.title: New to me: the Taskcluster team
entry.summary: Mozilla's Taskcluster manager explains taking on that team, and its priorities: redeployability, support for packet.net bare-metal and ARM hardware, and keeping the lights on.

entry.title: Shameless self (release) promotion: Firefox 53.0b1 from TaskCluster
entry.summary: Mozilla released Firefox 53.0b1 for Linux and Android from TaskCluster while Mac and Windows still came from buildbot, using the same task graph as nightly builds.

entry.title: Taskcluster: CI for Engineers
entry.summary: Mozilla removed Taskcluster's need for Azure and Heroku so it can be installed on Kubernetes outside Mozilla, and describes when the CI system is a good fit.

entry.title: Ontology-Driven Observability: Building an End-to-End Knowledge Graph at Netflix Scale
entry.summary: Netflix describes building an ontology-driven knowledge graph that links metrics, alerts, incidents, deployments and on-call data so incident investigations stop taking hours to reconstruct context.

entry.title: The Lifecycle of LLM-as-a-Judge: Building, Aligning, and Monitoring at scale
entry.summary: Netflix describes the lifecycle of an LLM judge for recommendation explanations, from human-labeled benchmarks and reasoning-aligned rubric tuning to deployment and weekly human monitoring.

entry.title: API Gateway and AI Gateway: Do You Need Both?
entry.summary: Nordic APIs compares API gateways and AI gateways on direction of traffic, caching, rate limiting, security and monitoring, and argues most companies building LLM applications need both.

entry.title: Agentic on the coach's couch: 24 questions, eight projects
entry.summary: OCTO built a 24-question assessment grid, scored from evidence in each repository, for eight AI-agent-assisted projects and proposes it as an extra input for team coaching diagnostics.

entry.title: Towards a model platform
entry.summary: OCTO describes a model platform for versioning, deploying, serving, monitoring and governing models, motivated by EU AI Act obligations, with the architecture options it compared.

entry.title: Introducing ModuleLens: Zooming into PyTorch Modules for Human and Agentic Engineering
entry.summary: Pinterest built ModuleLens, which captures inputs, weights and init arguments of PyTorch modules during training so any module can be reconstructed and debugged locally without multi-GPU setup.

entry.title: Open Source Profiler on an Internet Scale Fleet: Pinterest and Intel Partnership on gProfiler
entry.summary: Pinterest and Intel describe adopting and extending the open-source gProfiler for continuous profiling across hundreds of thousands of instances, including dynamic profiling and hardware counter flame graphs.

entry.title: Organizations need decision-grade knowledge. AI makes it urgent.
entry.summary: Stack Overflow explains the product decision behind Stack Internal, arguing that retrieval alone does not give answers people can act on and that experts should validate knowledge selectively.

entry.title: Part 1: Make your AI agents boring: the determinism layer
entry.summary: Part 1 of a Stack Overflow series on production LLM systems describes a determinism layer where agents only propose actions and fixed graphs, typed outputs and a ledger keep systems testable.

entry.title: Part 2: Evals as a deployment gate — and how to know when they drift
entry.summary: Part 2 of a Stack Overflow series on production LLM systems describes evals as a CI deployment gate plus baselines and shadow evals to catch drift.

entry.title: Part 3: Knowing when your agent doesn’t know: the confidence layer
entry.summary: Part 3 of a Stack Overflow series on production LLM systems describes composing calibrated confidence from several signals, sampling a judge model and routing uncertain decisions to humans.

entry.title: Part 4: Safety and governance for LLM systems: guardrails, PII, audit, and memory
entry.summary: Part 4 of a Stack Overflow series on production LLM systems describes layered fail-closed guardrails, PII redaction at boundaries, an immutable audit ledger and scoped multi-tenant memory.

entry.title: Part 5: Operating an LLM system: observability, cost, routing, and the platform underneath
entry.summary: Part 5 of a Stack Overflow series on production LLM systems specifies decision-level observability, cost control at a gateway chokepoint, model routing and fallback, a kill switch and identity.

entry.title: Part 6: An operating system for coding agents: the disciplined build
entry.summary: Part 6 of a Stack Overflow series describes a harness for coding agents, from a constitution file and autonomy boundary to tiered context, memory, review panels and decision logs.

entry.title: Why your platform team shouldn't build an AI context layer (even though they probably could)
entry.summary: Stack Overflow argues that platform teams should not build an internal AI context layer, because capture, validation, governance and delivery become ongoing maintenance costs.

entry.title: Why I tried to kill token billing (and why we kept it)
entry.summary: Metronome's author explains why token billing is a poor customer-facing price but useful backend infrastructure, and argues for unified credits and output-based pricing.

entry.title: Continuous Aggregate Refresh Policies for Solar and Wind SCADA Data: Choosing the Right Policy Shape
entry.summary: Timescale's guide explains how to read continuous aggregate refresh policies and choose among five policy shapes for solar and wind SCADA data, including retention and late data.

entry.title: "I'm Sorry, Have We Met?" — Frictionless Memory for AI
entry.summary: Trivago compares four approaches to AI chatbot memory, from resending the whole conversation to RAG over memories and a three-stage SimpleMem pipeline, using a concierge demo.

entry.title: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
entry.summary: Cloudflare rebuilt range-request caching on its Pingora-based cache to align origin fetches to disk chunks, roughly halving p99 time to first byte for R2 and cutting tiered cache traffic about 6%.

entry.title: Beyond API Compatibility: Building a Tool to Measure the Blast Radius of Library Changes
entry.summary: Netflix's Java Platform team built Quasar, which indexes code from CI builds into Parquet on S3 to show which repositories use API symbols that a library change affects.

entry.title: Localizing compliance at scale: achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification
entry.summary: Cloudflare obtained South Korea's ISMS certification and, to enforce itemized consent, removed social sign-up in South Korea rather than build a separate consent gate after authentication.

entry.title: Dark mode was never on our roadmap. Here’s how it got built.
entry.summary: One Medium web engineer built dark mode using CSS light-dark() tokens instead of caching separate light and dark copies, with a Statsig flag splitting the Cloudflare Workers edge cache during rollout.

entry.title: Single-tenant Titus: VM-level isolation on a multi-tenant container platform
entry.summary: Netflix added an allowlisted single-tenant mode to its Titus container platform that gives a task its own right-sized EC2 instance, after weighing shared-kernel tuning, microVMs, gVisor and plain EC2.

entry.title: Agentic harnesses (1/2): why yesterday's good practices are expensive today
entry.summary: The article argues that coding-agent harness practices built for weaker models, such as long AGENTS.md files and maximum reasoning, now cost more, using token prices and prompt-cache behaviour as worked examples.

entry.title: My agents were reading too much: what ten weeks of token hunting taught me
entry.summary: A product coach measured the billable tokens of his AI agents and applied seven measures, such as a 150-line CLAUDE.md cap, after which median tokens per launched agent fell 55%.

entry.title: We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment
entry.summary: Shopify built Remote Dev, a pool of warm remote Macs that AI agents claim over SSH to build and test its mobile apps, with Android emulators on separate Linux VMs.

entry.title: The Regression Tests Nobody Writes: Capturing How Software Actually Behaves
entry.summary: The article describes characterization tests and proposes recording a service's real network traffic, including database and queue calls, and replaying it to detect behaviour changes in long-lived systems.

entry.title: How Retention Policies Silently Break Continuous Aggregates
entry.summary: A TimescaleDB retention job that dropped raw chunks inside a continuous aggregate's refresh window made the next refresh silently delete buckets; the fix is one retention-versus-refresh invariant plus an audit query.

entry.title: Cloudflare deploys protections against php2shell vulnerability
entry.summary: Cloudflare deployed WAF protections against the php2shell PHP vulnerabilities about 9 hours before public disclosure, using full transaction detection that combines request and origin-response signals.

entry.title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
entry.summary: Commerce.com and Cloudflare enabled WebMCP agent tools across almost 100,000 storefronts with a per-merchant opt-out built from Configuration Rules and custom hostname metadata.

entry.title: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
entry.summary: Cloudflare added full transaction detection to its WAF, evaluating each request together with the origin's response, and response rules that can block a matching response.

entry.title: The Agents on Rails Files: designing black-box evals for coding agents
entry.summary: Evil Martians replaced hidden Rails tests with browser-based black-box checks for stage 3 of their Agents on Rails coding-agent benchmark and calibrated the grader with mutants.

entry.title: We built three memory systems. The most expressive one wasn’t the most useful.
entry.summary: Tiger Data built three memory systems for its Slack agent Eon, a fact list, a PostgreSQL knowledge graph and an ltree tree with hybrid search, and kept the tree.

entry.title: Use Scenario Tables to Identify Requirements
entry.summary: The author built a scenario table from the code of a nightly due-date sync job and reviewed it row by row with client staff, which exposed missing requirements.

entry.title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know
entry.summary: Cloudflare describes its response after private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised, including trust-store updates and CDN and Zero Trust mitigations deployed on October 20.

entry.title: How Hamlet uses Databricks Lakebase Postgres to test changes against production data
entry.summary: Hamlet moved pull request validation to Databricks Lakebase, where each pull request gets a copy-on-write branch of production data for its preview environment and AI coding agents.

entry.title: The Quiet Tax on Machine Learning Teams
entry.summary: Expedia Group built a CLI that scaffolds ML projects per business domain and copies shared infrastructure code into each project, to stop repeating CI/CD, permission and cluster setup for every model.

entry.title: The Technology Behind the Names: How We're Bringing Local War Memorials to Life
entry.summary: Findmypast linked military and census records into a graph, used embeddings for spelling variants and AI checks on newspaper articles to tell the stories behind names on over 9,000 WW1 memorials.

entry.title: How 3 Java Champions are using GitHub Copilot for increased productivity
entry.summary: Three Java Champions describe using GitHub Copilot, including migrating about 900 slides from Reveal.js to Marp and diagnosing a Pi4J virtual-thread pinning bug on a Raspberry Pi 4.

entry.title: App stability at scale with a layered defense
entry.summary: Grab describes layered release safety for its Android app: custom lint rules, tests, an early-access gate, staged rollouts that auto-pause on crashes, feature-flag kill switches and alerting.

entry.title: Cross-store product clustering across millions of stores
entry.summary: Shopify groups the same product across millions of stores under one global ID using embedding retrieval, a three-stage scorer cascade trained on LLM-judge labels and graph-based clustering.

entry.title: How Shopify turns open models into task experts
entry.summary: Shopify post-trains open models such as Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as task-specific subagents for Sidekick, using an LLM judge and nightly self-healing data, reporting faster responses and about 90% lower serving cost.

entry.title: Designing IIoT Ingest That Survives a Cut Uplink
entry.summary: A guide to an IIoT ingest path in PostgreSQL that replays buffered rows exactly once after an outage, using a unique constraint, a SQLite buffer and a rate-capped COPY replay.

entry.title: Observability At Scale — Every Byte Counts
entry.summary: Wise cut monthly observability spend by 40% through five changes, including lz4 for Loki chunks, zstd for traces, Prometheus Remote Write v2 and a larger query split interval.

entry.title: Spin-Up, Test, Tear-Down: How trivago Runs 600+ Preview Environments on Kubernetes
entry.summary: trivago runs 600+ per-PR preview environments on Kubernetes by deploying only the changed service with ArgoCD and scaling previews to zero with Kedify's KEDA HTTP add-on.

entry.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
entry.summary: Cloudflare cut its AI code reviewer's average cost per review from $2.43 to $0.77 with a shared prompt-cache prefix, fewer wasted LLM calls and model and effort experiments.

entry.title: GenRecs Tokenization: Transforming Ads Recommendation at Meta with Stable Model Vocabulary
entry.summary: Meta built GenRecs Tokenization, which quantizes multimodal item embeddings into shared codebook tokens for ads recommendation models, reporting a 0.35% conversion lift with GEM and the Adaptive Ranking Model.

entry.title: Inside Prometheus: Meta’s Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster
entry.summary: Meta describes Prometheus, its Ohio GPU supercluster on NVL72 racks, and the in-rack spares, per-replica fault tolerance and asynchronous checkpointing that cut training interruptions by 99%.

entry.title: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do
entry.summary: Meta replaced a single all-knowing agent for data column onboarding with a 1,300-line deterministic orchestrator that routes workflows to 14 specialist subagents, cutting preparation from days to under an hour.

entry.title: Local LLM on iOS 27: what Apple doesn't say in the docs
entry.summary: The author embedded Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct in an iOS 27 app via Core AI, measured launch time and schema compliance, and found Apple's system model faster on compatible iPhones.

entry.title: Building Overexposed: understanding application exposure
entry.summary: Shopify built Overexposed, a scanner that lists GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run services from Cloud Asset Inventory and probes each anonymously to find unintended public exposure.

entry.title: How to Run SQL Server Outside Docker Sandboxes
entry.summary: The author ran one SQL Server on the host for several Claude Code agents in Docker sbx sandboxes, giving each sandbox its own database name and forwarding a port with socat.

entry.title: Exploring OTP Patterns for Agentic Workflows
entry.summary: The first chapter on OTP patterns for agent workflows keeps each run's state in one GenServer and rebuilds it after a crash from an append-only log of goals, decisions and results.

entry.title: A pragmatic guide to AI-assisted development
entry.summary: The author used Claude Code with Opus 5.5 to trace and fix a bug in an internal scheduling tool, with separate sessions for implementation, review and verification, ending in a one-line change.

entry.title: On-Behalf-Of Is a Pattern. Token Exchange Is the Standard.
entry.summary: The article compares the On-Behalf-Of pattern, Microsoft's jwt-bearer flow and RFC 8693 Token Exchange for delegated API calls, and how each applies to AI agents.

entry.title: Continuous accountability for Verified bots
entry.summary: Cloudflare built a system that scores whether Verified bots keep following robots.txt and slow down after HTTP 429 responses, turning repeated behaviour into an explainable trust band.

entry.title: Flex Model: an event-driven feature engineering system
entry.summary: Jane Street replaced a monolithic feature system with Flex Model, an event-driven engine that turns market events into feature vectors using a fixed per-event plan built at startup.

entry.title: Agent rooms: the only place where you are happy to be contradicted
entry.summary: A product coach used twelve agent rooms in which AI agents with written roles gave positions and debated before he decided, and reports what the rooms caught and where they failed.

entry.title: Advancing Generative Recommendation Inference: our collaboration with NVIDIA on TensorRT LLM
entry.summary: Spotify and NVIDIA added beam search, embedding inputs and multi-item scoring to TensorRT LLM for Spotify's LLM podcast recommendations, reporting up to 54% lower beam search cost.

entry.title: A fully programmable secure web gateway
entry.summary: Cloudflare lets customers run Worker code inline in Cloudflare Gateway and DLP policy evaluation through a new Forward action, Custom Functions and DLP custom validation functions.

entry.title: Cloudflare and OpenAI: Making AI discovery better for everyone
entry.summary: Cloudflare and OpenAI ran a research pilot in which signals from Cloudflare's network helped OpenAI's search crawler discover and index new web pages for ChatGPT.

entry.title: How FactSet cut model training and deployment from days to hours with Databricks AI Runtime
